title: Four Seasons in Ottawa
body:
Ottawa is the capital of Canada, and it has got four very different seasons.

Winter is long and very cold, from December to March. It's often minus twenty degrees, and there's a lot of snow. People wear warm coats, hats and boots. In February the Rideau Canal freezes, and people skate on it to work!

Spring comes in April. The snow melts and the days get longer. In May there are thousands of tulips in the parks. Their colours are beautiful.

Summer is hot and humid. It's often thirty degrees. People swim in the lakes, eat ice cream and sit on patios.

In the fall, the leaves on the trees turn red, orange and yellow. The air is fresh and cool. It's my favourite season. But soon, winter is back again!

title: Life in Ennistymon
body:

What is there? There's one main street with colourful shops. There's a butcher, a chemist, a post office and a little bookshop. There are lots of pubs, and there's traditional Irish music most nights. There's a river with a beautiful waterfall, and the sea is only ten minutes away by car.

What isn't there? There's no cinema and no train station. There isn't a big supermarket, so we go to Ennis for the weekly shop. There are buses, but not many.

My cousins in Dublin think my town is boring. I don't agree. Everybody knows everybody here. When I walk down the street, people always say hello.

And at night, I can see the stars.
